answer: A bond of 56% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in anchor, and kernel reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 113 aliases, and each one needs its own funded lotus account. That bill is paid per identity, so 64 aliases cost 173 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
